analysis:
This pass examined the SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift head (lines 1-343) and two test files. Relevant threat: T-041, which relies on the 30-minute sliding TTL, LRU budget and whole-root sweep of darkbloom/kv3.

Changed behavior:
- The TTL pass now calls removeOwned(expired, unusedSince: now - ttl) (head lines 119, 127, 154). For a loaded store, SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries is told the cutoff, so it can keep a file whose in-index last hit is newer than the stale mtime scan. This matches the documented sliding-TTL semantics: a hit refreshes recency.
- Unloaded roots still delete every mtime-expired file via performUnloadedDestructiveChange (lines 138-143), which is unchanged.
- For files that survived the TTL pass, lines 161-165 re-read mtime through FileManager.attributesOfItem. This only affects LRU ordering in the budget loop. A failed read keeps the old (stale, older) mtime, which makes the file evicted earlier, not later. The budget loop still evicts until total <= limit, so the budget is not weakened.
- OwnedFile.modifiedAt changed from let to var (line 27); this is purely local.
- Header-ownership checks, no-follow directory checks and removeItemIfSafe are unchanged.

Tests:
- SSDCheckpointMaintenanceEpochTests line 83+ now touches the index at the idle time and still expects the file to expire.
- SSDCheckpointFileCoordinatorTests adds shared/exclusive modes, upgrade/downgrade and randomized exclusivity checks. These imply an SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator source change that is not in this batch.

No regression was identified locally.

Unverified contracts for integration:
1. SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries(unusedSince:) must keep only entries whose index last hit is >= the cutoff, and must still delete the rest. If it retains entries unconditionally, or based on caller-controlled recency, the TTL bound in T-041 could be exceeded.
2. The new shared-mode coordinator must preserve exclusivity of maintenance/retirement (tryAcquire) against readers, so deletion cannot race an in-progress read or commit.
3. Whether the index touch also updates file mtime, so restart freshness stays consistent with the comment at line 159.
